traits.stem_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Ariocarpus: Ariocarpus: plants erect, unbranched, deep-seated in the substrate. Roots taproots. Stem unsegmented, gray-green (yellow-green or purplish with age or stress), above-ground portion flat, concave, or weakly hemispheric, usually flush with soil surface and cryptic, strongly tuberculate, 0-2(-10) × [3-]5-10(-15) cm, hard, rigid, tough skinned; tubercles arranged in rosettes or mosaics, ± triangular, 8-20 × [3-]11-25 mm, hard, exposed faces of tubercles strongly differentiated from sides, prominently fissured [wrinkled, roughened, or nearly smooth]; areoles elongate, forming a wide woolly groove on each tubercle; areolar glands absent. Spines absent. Flowers diurnal, borne in axils of tubercles near stem apex, broadly funnelform to almost salverform, 1.5-5 × 1.5-5 cm; outer tepals brownish or greenish with pink tinge; inner tepals pink or magenta, 13-34 × 4-10 mm; ovary smooth (scales, hairs, and spines absent); stigma lobes 5-10, white. Fruits indehiscent, white or cream to pale greenish, spheric to clavate or cylindric, proximally or almost completely buried in copious wool of stem apex, 10-25 × 5-10 mm, scales and spines absent. The tubercles' relief, distinct, from their 'exposed faces ... strongly differentiated from sides'.
